title: Total Gap to Equal Values
statement:
You get an array nums. For every position i, add up the distances |i − j| to every other position j that holds the same value (nums[j] === nums[i]). If the value appears nowhere else, the total is 0.

Return an array out of the same length where out[i] is that total for position i.

examples.why: The 4s sit at 0, 2 and 3. Position 0: 2 + 3 = 5. Position 2: 2 + 1 = 3. Position 3: 3 + 1 = 4. The 7s at 1 and 4 are 3 apart.
Every value appears once, so there is nothing to measure against.
The ends are far from everyone (1 + 2 + 3), the middle positions are close to everyone (1 + 1 + 2).

hints: Positions with different values never affect each other. Group the positions by value first.
Inside one group the positions are sorted. For position p with c earlier positions summing to S, the distance to the earlier ones is c·p − S. The later ones work the same way from the other side.
Walk each group once, keeping a running prefix sum. With the group's total sum you also know the sum of the later positions.

explain.intuition:
Only equal values interact, so collect the positions of each value in a hash map; each list comes out sorted because you scan left to right. Now the problem is: given sorted positions p₀ < p₁ < …, find each one's total distance to the others.

For p_k, every earlier position is to its left, so the distance to all of them is k·p_k − (p₀ + … + p_{k−1}). Every later position is to its right: (p_{k+1} + … ) − (m − 1 − k)·p_k. A running prefix sum gives both in O(1), so each group costs O(its size) instead of O(size²). With all equal values, the quadratic version does 10¹⁰ steps.
steps: Build a map from value to the list of its positions, in increasing order.
For each list of length m, compute its total sum T and start prefix = 0.
For the k-th position p: left = k·p − prefix, right = (T − prefix − p) − (m − 1 − k)·p.
Write left + right into out[p], then add p to prefix.
pitfalls: Comparing every pair inside a group. One value repeated 100 000 times makes that quadratic.
Mixing up counts on the right side: there are m − 1 − k later positions, not m − k.
Overflow in 32-bit languages: totals reach about 5·10⁹, so use 64-bit integers.

solutions.title: Compare every pair
solutions.idea: For every position, scan the whole array for equal values and add the distances.

solutions.title: Group positions, then prefix sums
solutions.idea: Within each value's sorted positions, the distance to earlier ones is count·p − their sum, and to later ones is their sum − count·p.

followups: Do it in two passes over the array (left to right, then right to left) without building the groups.
Return, for each position, the distance to the nearest equal value instead of the total.
